fullText:
Agent-to-agent communication with a personal agent on top is wild. 

Wow. I underestimated how well models like Opus 5.5 can coordinate already. 

This opens a whole new set of experiences with agents.

But it takes a bit of tuning (automations, webhooks, system prompts, tooling, etc.) and retrieving context at the right time. 

I don't have a perfect setup yet, but I feel like I'm already living in the future. 

My agent team can do work (higher quality than I could imagine) at speeds I can't even keep up with. 

It's crazy how fast things have moved in about a year. 

I started with individual Claude Code sessions.

Then, just a couple of months later, I moved to multi-agent systems with subagents, parallelizing work. 

Then, a couple of months ago, I built a persistent, higher-level agent team, similar to Grok Bot. Of course, with my own agent orchestrator and a team of like 8 specialized bots (CFO, CSO, CTO, CMO, CCO, CoS, etc.)

Then, about a month ago, I started playing around with agent-to-agent communication with a personal agent. 

And I can tell you, most of the apps like Code and Claude Desktop are way behind. But they will catch up.

This is why I believe we should all be building our own agent orchestrator/harness. You need to personalize to what works for you, which creates an important edge. You can start with a fork; who cares. Start somewhere. 

It's just mind-blowing to see agents coordinate and do things on their own that would take a village or an entire org in some cases. 

Just sharing my raw thoughts here, but things will dramatically change again in the next couple of months, leading into next year. 

Sharing a snapshot of one of my personal agents, Clio (Chief Content Officer), doing research all day and putting together high-quality content to inform me on things I am interested in and things I am writing about on X.

fullText:
800 BILLION AGENTS = A HUGE DATA PROBLEM

Agents are going to outnumber humans.

Like 100 to 1.

This is a big challenge for mobile networks. And for AI infrastructure.

But it's also a problem for businesses, because:

1. MORE AGENTS WILL MAKE EVERY DATA PROBLEM WORSE.

People use AI in short bursts, but agents never stop working.

So they need a continuous flow of incoming quality data.

And teams of agents need shared data that is interoperable.

The data problem is going to get way worse.

2. DATA QUALITY IS THE NEW SCALE ADVANTAGE.

A business with 50 people will have as much productive capacity as one with 5,000 only human employees.

So scale advantages are no longer going to be about headcount.

But this only works if the agents have quality data.

I view data quality as the new scale advantage. 

And no, data network effects aren't real.

3. CONTEXT IS KING.

Ask an agent "What was the revenue growth last quarter?"

It can easily fail.

Because it does not know how revenue or a quarter is defined in your business.

Most deployments fail due to brittle workflows and a lack of contextual learning.

For agents to work, they need to be co-designed by IT and domain experts.

***TAKEAWAY FOR MANAGERS:

→ Give someone the job of pruning your data. Everyone knows how to add data, but almost nobody removes it, and quality drops as it sprawls.

fullText:
HUAWEI'S 500,000 CHIP ANSWER TO NVIDIA

There is lot of talk about Huawei’s new Mate 90 smartphone, which uses their LogicFolding chip design. 

But I think everyone is watching the wrong part of Huawei's AI stack. 

The most important innovations are in the AI Data Centers 

1. HUAWEI IS REBUILDING AI INFRASTRUCTURE AT SCALE.

Huawei’s new Atlas 960E SuperPoD has 4,096 NPUs working as one giant integrated computer.

And these can be combined into a SuperCluster with more than 500,000 NPUs.

That’s what’s coming this year.

They are matching Nvidia in large scale AI compute.

2. INTERCONNECT INNOVATIONS HAVE BEEN MAKING A BIG DIFFERENCE.

Huawei lacks the most powerful NVIDIA GPUs, so it links many weaker chips as peers with its UnifiedBus.

And in the 960E, they have used 5,500 new optical engines to replace more than 48,000 pluggable optical modules.

This drops latency and doubles fault free operating time.

3. MEMORY IS THE STORY NOBODY TALKS ABOUT.

The SuperPod system treats the memory on all chips as one shared pool of 1.1 petabytes.

Agents create exploding context, so Huawei extends the KV cache to SSD layers and a single cluster reaches 64 petabytes.

This whole AI architecture has been moving really fast for the past 1-2 years.

***TAKEAWAYS FOR MANAGERS:

→ Ask your infrastructure team whether latency and memory, not chips, are the real limits on your AI workloads.

→ Estimate how much context your planned agents will carry, then budget memory and storage before you scale them.

fullText:
My first visit to the @UN HQ for the @ScienceBoard_UN  Scientific Advisory Board annual retreat and meeting with the Secretary General António Guterres, the Under-secretary Guy Ryder, and the rest of the team. 

We discussed the importance of grounding everything we do in science and factuality, especially with challenges of misinformation we see at large scale today.

We discussed new topics for our scientific briefs, which have been a highlight for me personally. I enjoy a lot to be able to collaborate with the UN team on timely topics like #AI and #climate modeling, tipping points, green #chemistry etc.

I particularly enjoy the diversity of scientific topics covered, and how AI is making an impact in all these areas: AI that is not LLMs, but AI trained on data from the physical world and scientific applications. 

This silent revolution of AI in science is often missed by the public and I am very thankful for UN Scientific Advisory Board for shining light on this.
